title: The Canadian comeback
decision: Conditional reserve. The exact same-contract series supports all 25 windows and the frozen five has both positive and negative responses, but three cards form a one-point tie group and first-public timestamp review plus independent editorial approval remain open.

identity.question: Will the Liberal Party win the most seats in the next Canadian election?
identity.rulesSummary: YES if the Liberal Party wins the most House of Commons seats in the next Canadian general election. This is not a majority or popular-vote contract; a tie uses the provider's alphabetical rule, and an election not held by December 31, 2025 resolves NO.

audienceRationale: A familiar national election story moves from a leadership vacuum through a trade crisis, a new leader and a snap campaign. Players can understand the stakes without knowing Canadian prediction markets.
playRationale: The five cards are deliberately different: a candidate enters, a trade shock lands, the party chooses its leader, the election is called, and the government answers an auto-tariff crisis.
tension: The final event-window response is -5.55 percentage points and the auto-tariff response is +3.675 points; the launch, tariff-retaliation and leadership-win cards are within the unchanged one-point anchor and therefore tie. The result is playable as a conditional reserve but less differentiated than the primary candidates.

selectionFreeze.disclosure: Broad daily-median suitability statistics and the retained raw history were visible from the original research. No Canada five-event window scores were run before this freeze. The selection is significance-first and timestamps were not moved after scoring.

dataset.markPolicy: Project Polymarket convention: latest source price per UTC hour, treated as trade; no filling, interpolation, carried prices, or cross-contract splicing.

events.title: Mark Carney launches his Liberal leadership campaign
events.mechanism: A new nationally recognizable contender changes who can carry the governing Liberals into the election.

claims.text: Mark Carney publicly launched his campaign to lead the Liberal Party and become prime minister.

events.competingExplanation: The market had already opened after Trudeau's resignation, and tariff anxiety plus other leadership candidates were already in view.

events.title: Canada announces a response to the U.S. tariff order
events.mechanism: The trade shock creates a crisis-response test that can make the Liberals look protective of Canadian interests or responsible for economic harm.

claims.text: Canada announced 25% counter-tariffs on $155 billion of U.S. goods in response to the U.S. tariff order.

events.competingExplanation: The U.S. order, Trudeau's address, provincial reactions and general risk sentiment arrived together.

events.title: Mark Carney wins the Liberal leadership
events.mechanism: The party chooses the person who will lead the Liberals into the general election and removes succession uncertainty.

claims.text: Mark Carney won the Liberal Party leadership on the first ballot with 85.9% of the vote.

events.competingExplanation: Carney was already the front-runner, so the vote may confirm information already priced in; the trade war and election timing also overlap.

events.title: The Governor General dissolves Parliament and calls the election
events.mechanism: The constitutional trigger turns an open-ended leadership story into a defined campaign with an April 28 endpoint.

claims.text: The Governor General approved the dissolution of Parliament and election writs were issued on March 23, 2025.

events.competingExplanation: The election call was expected; campaign positioning, polls, tariff news and leader impressions were moving at the same time.

events.title: Carney announces Canada's response to U.S. auto tariffs
events.mechanism: A concrete response to a sector-specific trade shock tests whether the new Liberal government can protect workers while limiting damage to an integrated economy.

claims.text: Canada announced countermeasures including 25% tariffs on non-CUSMA-compliant U.S. vehicles and support for Canadian workers and businesses.

events.competingExplanation: The U.S. tariff itself, the election campaign, market-wide trade news and the government's broader support measures are inseparable from the announcement.

ending.text: The Liberal Party won the most seats in the April 28, 2025 federal election. The provider records the YES contract as resolved and closed after the election; this result is not a scored card.
